metadata_mapping: Existing concept schema and responsive SVG conventions; local content changes only, no navigation or publication action.

patterns.title: Congestion Problems
patterns.domain: Strategic and game-theoretic problems; shared-load costs, congestion externalities, and efficient allocation

sources.title: Rosenthal, A Class of Games Possessing Pure-Strategy Nash Equilibria (1973)
sources.supports: Finite congestion-game definition: finite players and strategies selecting resource subsets, additive costs, common resource-cost functions of user counts; pure equilibrium existence.
sources.read_method: Full original three-page paper read, including definition, road-network example, theorem, proof, and caveat about potential minimization.
sources.boundary: Existence is not efficiency, uniqueness, or a behavioral convergence forecast. The article makes no universal existence claim for weighted, dynamic, nonseparable, or user-specific congestion models.

sources.title: Frank Kelly, The Mathematics of Traffic in Networks
sources.supports: Wardrop’s 1952 equilibrium tradition, continuous-flow versus individual-user considerations, total network delay, and congestion-pricing principles.
sources.read_method: Author-hosted Princeton Companion to Mathematics chapter proof retrieved and read locally, especially routing, Wardrop equilibrium, and total-delay/pricing sections. Web fetching timed out, but local retrieval succeeded.
sources.boundary: The chapter’s divisible-flow calculus pricing formula is not copied into the four-player model. An earlier numerical consistency check derived a discrete fee from the delay imposed on other users; that derivation is historical, not part of the current qualitative article. The current example states the incentive conditions for the proposed charge without specifying a formula. Wardrop’s original 1952 paper was identified but not obtained; the historical account is sourced through Kelly.

sources.title: City of Stockholm, Facts and Results from the Stockholm Trial, Final Version December 2006
sources.supports: Original evaluation of traffic counts, travel times, public transport, comparison difficulties, and distributional effects during the 2006 congestion-charge trial.
sources.read_method: Report’s authorship, methodological caveats, and traffic-results sections read, including printed pages 3–9.
sources.boundary: Before/during evaluation of a real policy bundle, with seasonal measurement issues, fuel-price changes, transit changes, and uneven route effects. Article transfers no numerical city effect to the commuter model and makes no randomization or universal causal effect-size claim.

patterns.short_description: Recognize when individually attractive choices crowd a shared resource, then distinguish the cost a user experiences from the additional delay imposed on others.
use_when: Which delay does the switching commuter leave to others?
goals: Recognize the familiar situation and preserve the defining mechanism.
Distinguish formal assumptions, empirical findings, and hypothetical continuations.
Make intervention authority, opportunity costs, and remaining constraints explicit.
mechanisms: Attach imposed delay to the route choice, or allocate access through a feasible alternative.
Measurement, collection, differing means, access, and diversion matter. No road capacity is added.

example_structure.scenario: Small group of commuters chooses shortcut or detour for a fixed departure window; own effects are noticeable. Private saving from a switch is smaller than combined imposed delay by assumption. Finite-user game separated from negligible-user Wardrop model. Hypothetical load-dependent charge needs measurement, collection, common time valuation, and stability of the proposed allocation. Fixed-demand mechanism distinguished from induced demand.
example_structure.changed_relationship: Attach imposed delay to the route choice, or allocate access through a feasible alternative.
example_structure.residual_constraints: Measurement, collection, differing means, access, and diversion matter. No road capacity is added.
example_structure.comparison: Qualitative choices, dependencies, and consequences; no invented scores, computed trajectory, or measured improvement claimed.

visual.question: Which delay does the switching commuter leave to others?
visual.alternative_text: Hypothetical qualitative illustration. A commuter switching to the shortcut saves personal time while existing shortcut users together incur more added delay. A load-dependent charge can attach that external cost to the decision. Roads, travelers, and the departure window stay fixed in the illustration. Change: Attach imposed delay to the route choice, or allocate access through a feasible alternative. Limitation: Measurement, collection, differing means, access, and diversion matter. No road capacity is added.
visual.caption: Hypothetical illustration. The two upper cards compare the switcher’s saving with others’ combined delay without inventing travel times. A charge changes private decision cost rather than capacity. It requires defensible measurement and the example’s common valuation of time; longer-term induced demand is a separate mechanism.
